lede: TSMC's A14 roadmap reveal is the day's defining story, locking in a 2028 production target that keeps the foundry a node ahead of Samsung and Intel. Meanwhile, machine learning placement tools continue their march into mainstream EDA flows.

stories.headline: TSMC commits A14 node to 2028 production
stories.summary: At its technology symposium, TSMC laid out the A14 process roadmap with production slated for 2028, claiming a 15 percent speed gain over N2 at equal power. The node pairs second-generation nanosheet transistors with a new standard cell architecture aimed at AI accelerators. CoWoS packaging capacity is also set to double next year.
stories.why_it_matters: The announced schedule keeps TSMC roughly a full node ahead of Samsung and Intel Foundry, which shapes where every major AI chip lands through the decade.

stories.headline: Nvidia's B300 accelerator targets datacenter refresh cycles
stories.summary: Nvidia introduced the B300 accelerator at GTC with higher HBM capacity and a revised NVLink topology. Early cloud partners are already listing instances for the first half of next year.
stories.why_it_matters: Each accelerator generation resets the economics of training clusters, and B300 supply will determine who can scale next year.

stories.headline: Cadence ships reinforcement learning placement in Innovus
stories.summary: Cadence added a reinforcement learning placement engine to Innovus, reporting single-digit PPA gains on customer testcases. The feature moves ML placement from research demos into a mainstream production flow.
stories.why_it_matters: Production EDA adoption is the real signal that AI-assisted physical design has crossed from papers into tapeouts.
